saturation_history.rationale: The taxonomy covers the monitored signals, evaluation references, detector types, feedback, adaptation, release containment, and training-serving topology. It therefore subsumes most codes, including red-teaming, shadow evaluation, reward-hacking detection, process supervision, safety monitoring, drift metrics, and rollback as choices of signals, validation methods, detection mechanisms, or containment actions. However, the minibatch also contains a distinct observability-pipeline axis: how telemetry is instrumented, collected, aggregated, visualized, and integrated with infrastructure and offline-RL analysis. Prometheus/Grafana choices and detailed latency, outcome, feature-presence, and safety instrumentation are not merely choices of which signals to select; they concern the monitoring data-plane and observability tooling. The taxonomy has no dimension for this implementation architecture. In addition, the checkpoint-healing codes introduce a distinct runtime recovery-control policy: when performance is sampled, how degradation baselines and thresholds are defined, how checkpoints are created and selected, and how learning is modified after recovery. Existing release containment covers rollback and model restoration at a high level, but it does not capture these adaptive in-training healing decisions without conflating release containment with performance-recovery control. Codes describing reward shaping/model architecture, generic outcomes, governance documentation, and broad risks are either covered by existing objective/feedback dimensions or are not themselves monitoring-infrastructure design decisions.

All relevant open codes are subsumed by existing taxonomy dimensions. Human feedback, contextual adaptation, annotation, calibration, and escalation fit Feedback Modality, Objective Validation Strategy, and Approval Protocol. Tool-conditioned state segmentation, exposure proportions, reference-policy support, drift metrics, aggregate-metric limitations, and episodic or non-Markov signal handling fit Production Monitoring Signal Selection and Anomaly Detection Architecture. Reward hacking, process filtering, verifiers, rubrics, co-optimization, optimization horizons, scalable oversight, and chain-of-thought monitoring fit Reward and Process Verification Strategy, Anomaly Detection Architecture, Objective Validation Strategy, and Safety Filtering Strategy. Data/model drift, retraining, continual pre-training, retrieval augmentation, human correction, dashboards, and automated upkeep fit Update Cadence and Trigger, Update Implementation Strategy, and Production Monitoring Signal Selection. Deployment APIs, shadowing, canaries, safety gates, rollback, and SLOs fit Training and Serving Topology, Release Exposure Strategy, Recovery and Version Control, and Governance and Transparency Controls. Novel-situation detection, capability estimation, hazardous-state recognition, and alarm raising are variants of anomaly detection, safety filtering, and objective validation. The remaining codes describe forces, outcomes, or implementation variants of these existing axes rather than distinct architectural decisions requiring a new dimension.

Most open codes are subsumed by existing dimensions: reward and verifier variants fit Reward and Process Verification Strategy; drift, baselines, alerting, and OOD monitoring fit Production Monitoring Signal Selection or Anomaly Detection Architecture; feedback workflows fit Feedback Modality and Governance and Transparency Controls; rollout, shadowing, canaries, rollback, and fallback behavior fit Release Exposure Strategy, Recovery and Version Control, and Safety Filtering Strategy; and retraining, topology, access control, and orchestration fit the existing update, topology, and governance dimensions. However, schema/data-quality validation at telemetry or trajectory ingestion, including the choice to fail fast on malformed data, is a distinct architectural decision. It governs whether corrupted monitoring/training data is admitted into the pipeline and how ingestion behaves on validation failure. The existing feature-presence monitoring and dataset/version-control dimensions do not capture this ingestion-validation and failure-mode axis without conflating signal selection with data-integrity gating.

The open codes are subsumed by existing taxonomy dimensions. Reward-hacking diagnosis, verification, documentation, exploit patching, anti-hacking constraints, adversarial testing, evaluation-suite expansion, and reward-function iteration are covered by Reward and Process Verification Strategy, Objective Validation Strategy, Anomaly Detection Architecture, and Update Implementation Strategy. Chain-of-thought versus action-only monitoring, cross-metric divergence, output-quality checks, drift signals, and behavior-pattern monitoring are alternatives within Production Monitoring Signal Selection and Anomaly Detection Architecture. Held-out evaluation, changing distributions, uncertainty, partial observability, multi-agent interaction, sparse rewards, safe exploration, and deployment resilience can be represented through Objective Validation Strategy, Anomaly Detection Architecture, Safety Filtering Strategy, and Release Exposure Strategy. Training and Serving Topology covers placement and connectivity but does not subsume these alternative serving-optimization mechanisms or their throughput-latency-alignment trade-offs. The affected-period dataset-ingestion freeze also exposes a distinct incident data-containment decision—whether and how to quarantine suspect production data before it feeds retraining—which is not captured by model rollback, version control, or general telemetry governance.

Most open codes are subsumed by existing dimensions: telemetry and feedback choices fit Production Signal Selection; statistical tests, activation classifiers, reasoning traces, and human or adversarial checks fit Anomaly Detection Architecture or Reward Verification Strategy; reward hacking, proxy divergence, and safety-related objectives fit Reward Construction Strategy; and checkpoint restoration, fine-tuning, continued training, rollout, and rollback fit the update and recovery dimensions. The Ray/SageMaker and cost/productivity codes describe general RL platform selection rather than monitoring architecture and are therefore not relevant to this design space. However, the codes concerning CMDP feasibility guarantees, environment-specific safety budgets, and adaptive Lagrangian enforcement reveal a distinct architectural decision: how deployment-time safety constraints are represented and enforced, including static modeled constraints versus adaptive observed-cost penalties. This axis is not captured by reward construction alone without conflating reward specification with constraint-enforcement/control architecture. Associated distribution-shift and stale-signal risks are outcomes already absorbable under drift detection, OOD verification, and anomaly monitoring.

The taxonomy covers the monitored signals, detection methods, evaluation strategies, update loops, serving topology, rollout, and recovery decisions represented by most open codes. However, it does not yet capture a distinct decision about the integration and operational delivery of monitoring capabilities: embedded callback versus external diagnostics layer, command-line/reporting interfaces, and metadata/API-based run traceability. It also lacks a telemetry-capture and retention architecture dimension covering endpoint capture, payload/metadata persistence, storage destination and partitioning, and subsequent inspection workflows. Finally, least-privilege access control, secrets management, and model-artifact vulnerability scanning introduce a security-governance axis for the monitoring and deployment infrastructure that cannot be absorbed by safety constraints, serving topology, or rollback without conflating distinct decisions. Other codes, including S3-stored request/response data as signals, SLOs, offline and counterfactual evaluation, reward-hacking tests, feedback-driven updates, policy freezing, guardrails, and framework/topology choices, are subsumed by existing dimensions.

All relevant open codes are subsumed by existing dimensions. Logging-related codes—including behavior-policy observability, trajectory completeness, partitioned trajectory storage, model-action logging, feature consistency, and telemetry collection—fit Production Signal Selection and Training and Serving Topology. Offline policy evaluation, importance sampling, fitted-Q evaluation, conservative objectives, replay, simulation, shadow evaluation, and stress testing fit Behavioral Verification Method, Statistical Detection Test, and Release and Recovery Control. Drift, support divergence, OOD degradation, novelty detection, uncertainty, and safety-generalization concerns fit Statistical Detection Test and Safety Constraint Strategy. Shadowing, canarying, A/B testing, registries, promotion gates, continuous deployment, checkpoints, autoscaling, and rollback or circuit-breaker mechanisms fit Release and Recovery Control, Inference Serving Strategy, Training and Serving Topology, and RL Platform Selection. Reward hacking, evaluator gaming, concealment, trip wires, sandboxing, proxy-reward blind spots, and capability-driven failures fit Reward-Hack Detection Architecture, Reward Construction Strategy, Behavioral Verification Method, and Reasoning Monitoring Method. Human oversight, handover, feedback, continual learning, and compliance or auditability fit Release and Recovery Control, Update Data and Adaptation Strategy, and the existing access-control and audit-related topology values. The remaining codes mostly describe forces, risks, outcomes, implementation examples, or specific values along these existing axes rather than independent architectural decisions.
